utility.value: Xcel Energy or United Power, check your electric bill
utility.notes: United Power lists Brighton among the cities and towns it serves. Xcel Energy's Colorado Communities Served list (10/2015) shows Brighton with gas and electricity service. Both Xcel Energy and United Power list Brighton among the communities they serve. United Power says its service area is in two noncontiguous areas, the plains northeast of Denver and two mountain canyons. Neither utility's list says which Brighton addresses it serves, and the City's pages give no address lookup. Check the utility named on your electric bill, or call United Power Member Services at 303-637-1300.

value.name: Xcel Energy or United Power (the utility that serves your address)
value.notes: The utility that serves your address supplies its electricity. Check the utility named on your electric bill.

county.notes: The City's permit pages do not state which county a Brighton address is in.

permit_authority.notes: The City's Community Development department handles permitting and inspections, and its Building Permit Counter takes questions at 1stop@brightonco.gov or 303-655-2017. Community Development functions, including permitting and inspections, end at noon on Fridays. The City's Permitting page links to Adams County GIS and Weld County GIS. The City's permit pages do not say how to confirm that an address is inside Brighton city limits, so ask the Building Permit Counter before you apply. The City's Brighton Solar page does not list the plans or documents to upload with a solar permit application. Ask the Building Permit Counter what to upload before you apply.

permit_url.notes: The City's Brighton Solar page says new and existing OpenGov users must apply for permits on the solar page. A new user signs up, obtains a license, and then begins the solar permitting process. To apply for a permit or contractor's license, you create an account through OpenGov.

interconnection_url.notes: This link is for United Power members. United Power asks you to review its Solar Interconnection Standards and Terms & Conditions before signing a contract with a solar installer, then submit its online application with your solar contractor. Members must sign the United Power Interconnection Terms and Conditions. United Power engineers review solar installations connecting to the grid to ensure the grid can accommodate them. Systems connected without proper notification to United Power will be immediately disabled. United Power rolls excess kWh over to the next month at the member's applicable rate, and a member that still has excess generation at the end of the annual April to March period is cashed out at the wholesale energy rate. For Xcel Energy customers, Xcel's interconnection page is https://co.my.xcelenergy.com/s/renewable/developers/interconnection. Xcel says that in most cases the developer or installer submits the application on your behalf, or you can manage your own. Xcel highly recommends that construction of your system should not commence until your application receives full approval from the Xcel Energy engineering team and all final agreements are fully signed. Xcel says its interconnection work ends with a permission to operate letter from Xcel to the generator owner. The utility's approval to operate is separate from the City permit and the City's inspections.

value.name: Renewable Battery Connect
value.description: Xcel says that when you add an eligible solar charged battery to your home or small business and participate, you let Xcel automatically manage your battery during periods of peak demand on the grid. Upfront incentive, General: $250 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to $5,000 per application). Income Qualified: $1,000 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to 75% of the equipment-only cost). Disproportionately Impacted Community: $500 per kW AC of Max Continuous Discharge Power (up to 75% of the equipment-only cost). There is also a $100 annual participation incentive for all customer types for participating in control events (for 5 years).
value.eligibility: An Xcel Energy program for a home or small business that adds an eligible solar charged battery. Xcel says eligible solar battery equipment includes all Tesla Powerwall models or all current Enphase models. It is for Xcel Energy customers, so check which utility serves your address first.

battery_programs.notes: Amounts are from Xcel's Renewable Battery Connect page, which shows a 2026 General incentive budget with budget available, on figures dated 11/02/2026. United Power says that at this time it does not offer a rebate for new system installations. United Power handles a battery like a new solar installation, with a review of its interconnection Terms & Conditions and an online application.

required_documents.notes: The City's Brighton Solar page does not list the plans or documents to upload with a solar permit application. Ask the Building Permit Counter what to upload before you apply. For design criteria, the solar page sends applicants to the City's Codes and Information page. The City's design criteria sheet gives a ground snow load of 35 PSF and a wind design speed of 107 mph. The City reviews and enforces the 2023 National Electrical Code.

value: Apply for the solar permit in OpenGov on the City's solar page. A new user signs up and obtains a license first.
Once the permit is paid for, print the approved City stamped plans and permit card from the portal and keep them on site for the inspector.

Request rough inspections through the portal and upload the required photos into OpenGov: front of house and address, roof flashing, hold-downs, rail system, junction boxes, bonding and any required structural upgrades.

Contractors must schedule inspections in the portal, until 11:00 PM for the next business day (the page gives a 3:30 PM cutoff for single family unit inspections). Homeowners may call the inspection line at 303-655-2151 by 4:00 PM for next business day inspection.
Receive written approval from the building inspector before proceeding with the next step of construction.

United Power members (United Power's terms for inverter-based systems no larger than 25 kW): after construction, have the system inspected or certified by the local electrical wiring inspector with jurisdiction and return the Certificate of Completion to United Power. United Power inspects within ten business days after receiving it, or the witness test is deemed waived unless the parties agree otherwise.

Xcel Energy customers: after approval and signed agreements, Xcel works with you and your contractors to witness test and energize the system, and issues a permission to operate letter to the generator owner.
inspection_steps.notes: The City's solar page describes rough inspections and does not describe a final inspection for a solar permit. For questions about required inspections, the City says to call 303-655-2017. Inspectors cannot enter an occupied home without a person 18 years or older present. Passing the City's inspections is not the utility's approval to operate.

timeline_days.notes: The City's Review Times list says solar permits get rapid review and gives no number of days. The City says Building Division inspections are generally next day.

value.program_or_pathway: City solar permit, applied for in OpenGov on the City's solar page
other_conditions: A contractor license from the City is required to perform any work for which a license is authorized.
The City's Class E Specialty Trades license covers solar energy collection/conversion systems but does not authorize electrical work.

The City's Electrical Contractor license is issued to an individual, or a business employing in a supervisory capacity an individual, holding a current and valid State Master's Electrical License. Electrical contractors must also register with the City.

Contractor license and Electrical Code registration applications are made at OpenGov, and a contractor must furnish a certificate of general liability insurance in favor of the City. Licenses are valid for twelve months from the date of issue.
The City's licensing rules except an owner performing work on his or her own personal residence. Ask the Building Permit Counter before doing solar electrical work yourself.
United Power: system generation can not exceed 200% of the annual usage at that location.
United Power: the contractor installing your solar panels must place a disconnect switch and production meter housing on the side of your home.
Xcel Energy net metering: you must be an Xcel Energy residential or business electricity customer, and the name on the application must match the name on the Xcel Energy account or bill.

Xcel Energy net metering: expected generation, combined with other distributed generation serving the service address, must not exceed 200% of historical consumption (the previous 12 months at the time of application submission).
Xcel Energy net metering: all equipment must be UL 1741 SB certified and listed within the Solar Equipment Lists on the California Energy Commission website.

United Power members: under United Power's terms for inverter-based systems no larger than 25 kW, you may proceed to construct the system when United Power approves the interconnection request and returns it to you.

United Power members: the same terms require general liability insurance with a combined single limit of at least $300,000 for each occurrence, with certificates furnished to United Power before the system first operates.

eligibility_constraints.notes: License conditions are from the City's Contractor Licensing page. Size, equipment and account conditions are each utility's own and apply only to its customers.

permit_fees.notes: The City's 2026 fee schedule (effective January 1, 2026, amended by Resolution 2025-87) says all permits are processed based on valuation (estimated project materials and labor) unless otherwise specified. The schedule lists no fee specific to solar permits, so ask the Building Permit Counter how your solar permit fee will be set. For a valuation of $2,001.00 to $25,000.00, the permit fee is $69.25 for the first $2,000.00 plus $14.00 for each additional $1,000.00 or fraction thereof. For $25,001.00 to $50,000.00, it is $391.25 for the first $25,000.00 plus $10.10 for each additional $1,000.00 or fraction thereof. For $50,001.00 to $100,000, it is $643.75 for the first $50,000.00 plus $7.00 for each additional $1,000.00 or fraction thereof. Permits that require a review are assessed a plan review fee equal to 65% of the permit fee, payable at permit issuance. City use tax is 3.75% of 50% of the project valuation. All credit card transactions are charged an additional fee of 2.9% of the total amount due.

value.description: Xcel says customers who qualify under the terms of Income Qualified can receive an upfront rebate of $3 per watt of installed solar up to 10kW AC.
value.eligibility: Must be an Xcel Energy residential or business electricity customer and qualify under Xcel's Income Qualified terms.

value.name: Solar*Rewards Disproportionately Impacted Communities upfront rebate
value.description: Xcel says Disproportionately Impacted Communities can receive an upfront rebate of $0.50 per watt of installed solar up to 10kW AC.
value.eligibility: Must be an Xcel Energy residential or business electricity customer. The rebate is for Disproportionately Impacted Communities.

rebates.notes: These are Xcel Energy programs for Xcel customers. Xcel's page says that as of 10/05/2026 it moved $1,050,000 from Solar*Rewards C&I to the Solar*Rewards Residential IQ/DIC program. United Power says it does not offer a rebate for new system installations at this time. The City's Brighton Solar and Energy Efficiency pages describe no City rebate for residential solar.
